layout.desktop: Width >1100px AND height >600px: 100dvh fixed workspace, 68px toolbar, 1440px content maximum, 12px padding/gap; minmax(0,25fr) minmax(0,30fr) minmax(0,45fr) columns for lesson/instructions/hints, challenge and editor. The concept article expands at its natural height and pushes activity instructions and hints down; only the whole guide content scrolls, never a nested article slot.
layout.compact: Width 951–1100px AND height >600px: folded guide across the full row, 44px header, expanded content max-height 180px with scroll; stage/editor use 44/56 proportions.
layout.stacked: Width <=950px OR height <=600px: three rows for guide, stage and editor; page scroll beneath sticky toolbar; guide collapsed until opened or a hint request; tile surround clamp(320px,calc(100vw - 24px),560px), editor 560px.
layout.drawer: All learning surfaces: drawer overlays the workspace; main margin-left 0 and width 100%, without a reserved desktop 280px. Desktop remains nonmodal navigation; existing narrow-screen backdrop and focus trap are unchanged.
layout.toolbar: Portrait <=700px: 108px two-row toolbar. Other narrow viewports retain 56px base; wide short viewports retain 68px learning override.
layout.entry: 1160px maximum; two columns, 16px gaps; one column <=700px. Card padding 22px/18px; mascot wells 88px/64px.
layout.supersedes: The three-column/folded/stacked learning workspace replaces the prior 1.05:1 stage/editor layout and reserved desktop drawer space. Earlier .8:1.5 and 750px container rules remain superseded for active learning; ordinary lesson reading retains inherited layout.

geometry.blockly: Native connected silhouettes, start cap, statement notches and loop/conditional cavities; no imitation block geometry.
geometry.atlas: Transparent 3-column by 2-row six-slot atlas indexed at 300% 200%: path, hedge, rocks, water/obstacle, character, destination.

learningWorld.stage: Mission/goal, world/destination strip, live character and semantic collision map; Rows & columns, text board and position announcements. Play stays below stage. Square map centred on plain white with a thin learning-line outline, no map shadow or decorative world-scenery strips.
learningWorld.motion: 10 October: inner keyed 460ms character steps retain outer 360ms coordinate translation. Byte bobs, Dash hops, Gigi scampers, Fix trots, Milo swings/hops, Nova bounds; shadow, dust, goal and water ripples run locally. Successful route arrival gets 900ms before star feedback, with bounded dance/light/sparks and static success colour/status. Offscreen/hidden stages pause animations. Saved/system reduced motion removes spatial effects. Gesture-unlocked local startup/arrival sounds obey mute; Milo uses synthesized vowel-like chatter. Drawing sways around the pencil tip.
learningWorld.loading: Initial HTML and lazy learning-route fallback use the approved K mark's exact three paths, assembled in three 1800ms cycles with 100ms stagger then settled. System reduced motion is static. Actual loading only; no artificial delay. Sources: public/brand/mark-loading.svg, public/brand/loading.css, src/LoadingScreen.tsx, index.html.
learningWorld.guide: Concept prose and worked example, authored instructions and progressive hints share the activity guide. First challenge concept auto-opens only at wide desktop; later concepts start closed. Generic generated grade context is omitted, authored instructions retained and identical instruction/goal appears once within the guide. Narration stays opt-in and reads complete concept prose. Hint requests expand the folded guide and bring the heading into view; existing hint/star accounting and protected bests remain.
learningWorld.palette: Native Blockly flyout scale is fixed at .95, independent of height fitting. Long lists use native flyout scrolling and reflow on resize. Program canvas fitting, editable long-program overview and pointer/drag gesture stability remain.
learningWorld.drawing: Shared three-column/folded/stacked challenge shell and editor; smooth white paper, dotted target, Dash with pencil, progressive ink and heading pointer. Drawing work saves separately.

Latest layout review: ship only for the P2 article-space correction and drawer-overlay addition; refreshed Byte/Grade 2/Text/Drawing show readable prose, complete narration and reachable instructions/hints, with no material fix regression observed. Supplied checks: initial final 30 browser checks, correction batch 21 checks, then 3 drawer-geometry checks across desktop/phone/tablet passed. Latest build passed with 106.42KB CSS and known 837.08KB app/Blockly chunk warning; latest unit rerun passed all 935 tests across fourteen files in 8.81 seconds after the UI corrections. Scoped detector returned [] before/after the initial layout work, before the final review fix; not rerun here. No whole-platform, curriculum or accessibility certification is implied. narrative.overview:
A friendly K assembled from coding blocks connects making with play. Violet, teal and yellow carry the identity against ink lettering and cloud backgrounds. The approved extension adds a consistent mark, wordmark and heading voice to the existing learning application.

The working surface stays legible and task-focused: a quiet lesson or mission heading, a visible execution stage, and a block editor. Flat geometry and rounded corners support the playful identity without competing with the learner's program.

The approved 9 October learning extension makes each coding activity a playable top-down tile world. Deep purple navigation frames white workspaces on pale lavender ground; the live mascot, walkable path, obstacles and destination share one meaningful map. The same shell carries grade selection, lessons, Blockly and bounded typed practice; drawing changes the stage to smooth white paper with Dash's pencil.

The approved learning layout keeps lesson, activity instructions and progressive hints beside a smaller execution stage and the editor. Wide screens devote 25/30/45 of the workspace columns to those roles. The article expands in normal flow, pushing activity instructions and hints down within one scrollable guide column. The square map is centred on white, and the native Blockly palette keeps readable targets as the workspace changes size. The course drawer overlays the learning workspace without moving its panels.
keyCharacteristics: Fredoka for the wordmark and principal course heading; system type for reading and controls.
Light bordered workspaces and a dark course drawer.
Purple learning navigation and readable white workspaces around semantic mascot tile worlds.
A persistent wide-screen lesson guide, smaller stage and readable native Blockly palette.

rules.name: The Accent Legibility Rule
rules.body: Bright brand teal and yellow are identity accents, not small text colors on white; retain functional teal for readable block labels.

rules.name: The Semantic Terrain Rule
rules.body: Every painted obstacle inside the playable map represents a collision cell; a walkable tile represents open ground. Decorative scenery outside the map never creates a second route or hidden collision rule.

rules.name: The Reading Voice Rule
rules.body: Preserve the plain system face for instructions and controls. The tagline is exactly “Play. Build. Learn.”

rules.name: The Mark Integrity Rule
rules.body: Never stretch, rotate, relight or add an extra play triangle to the mark. Keep clear space of at least one quarter of its height. Use the normal symbol at 24 CSS pixels or larger; use the backed favicon below that. Use a tagline lockup at 260px wide or larger and omit the tagline for smaller placements.

dos: Do reuse the approved three-piece K and the exact tagline.
Do preserve system typography for lesson reading and controls.
Do keep focus, text scaling and reduced-motion behavior visible in new work.
Do use the darker functional teal for white movement-block labels.
Do apply learning tokens only within the learning shell and entry; preserve public-page rules and the master mark.
Do keep Play below the stage, real Blockly geometry, meaningful obstacle tiles and readable board alternatives.
Do preserve the shared white-paper drawing shell and Grade 1–6 entry choices.
Do keep native palette blocks at .95 scale and let long flyout lists scroll.
Do keep lesson prose, authored instructions and hints reachable within the responsive activity guide.
donts: Don't substitute a generic code icon for the approved mark.
Don't use bright teal or yellow as small text on white.
Don't stretch the logo or add lighting effects or a variant-only triangle.
Don't treat this brand extension as permission to redesign the learning flow.
Don't replace collision data with a decorative complete-scene background or change saved learners' routes.
Don't imply that mascot artwork implements formal Events, full Python, new accounts or curriculum validation.
